note: Recorded by hand from data/pages/config__latest__developerguide__config-region-support.md before the parser was written. Counted the data rows of the single table under 'List of Supported Regions', whose lead sentence is 'The following table lists the AWS Regions where you can enable AWS Config.' The table has 36 data rows (snapshot lines 39-74), read from the 'Region' column (the Region code), not from the endpoint hostname; rows with two endpoint lines (the four US Regions with a FIPS endpoint) are still one Region each. All 36 codes exist in regions.json, so nothing is unresolved. The 10 Regions in regions.json the table never names (cn-north-1, cn-northwest-1, eu-isoe-west-1, eusc-de-east-1, us-iso-east-1, us-iso-west-1, us-isob-east-1, us-isob-west-1, us-isof-east-1, us-isof-south-1) are simply absent: the page never says AWS Config is unavailable there, so they are not exclusions and derivation stays 'enumerated'. The 'Considerations' section names AWS Config sub-features (resource types, managed rules, organizational rules, conformance packs, remediation actions, aggregators, advanced queries, the natural language query processor) as supported in a subset of Regions, but it gives no Region lists — only links to other pages. Those are pointers, not coverage: no feature is emitted for any of them, and they do not make any listed Region 'partial', because this feature counts where AWS Config can be enabled. So every row is 'full' and there are no partials or exclusions.
